strengths: Clear identification and formalization of the sampling wall problem, providing valuable conceptual contribution beyond the proposed solution
Simple and elegant solution requiring minimal architectural modifications, making it practical for adoption
Substantial empirical improvements in generation quality (55-61% Gen PPL reduction) across multiple datasets and model types
Exceptionally comprehensive experimental validation including multiple datasets, metrics, ablations, and matched computational budget analysis
Thorough investigation of what the method addresses (idle steps, oscillations) with exploration/exploitation phase analysis
Honest reporting including negative results (e.g., LDDM-U limited improvements, multi-step backprop failure) and careful experimental design
weaknesses: Lacks rigorous theoretical foundation for why latent pathway propagation helps; the connection to RNNs is mentioned but unexplored, and the design appears empirically driven rather than principled
Non-trivial computational cost (~30% training time increase, doubled embeddings) not fully justified given the improvements; matched budget experiment incompletely addresses this concern
Significant scalability concerns: experiments only on moderately-sized academic models; no evidence of effectiveness on large-scale models (billions of parameters)

Self-conditioning design raises alignment concerns: stop-gradient is justified post-hoc (D.5), and multi-step backpropagation dramatically hurts performance (Table 11), suggesting training objective may not match inference
Uneven improvements across variants: strong for MDLM but marginal for UDLM on zero-shot tasks; LDDM-M's strong downstream performance on LAMBADA but not other tasks raises generalization questions
Generation quality evaluated primarily via proxy metrics (Gen PPL with GPT-2, G-eval with GPT-4.1); no human evaluation despite claims of improved coherence
Limited investigation into what is actually propagated: does not empirically compare h_t vs x_θ,t, and D.3 shows MLP augmentation provides minimal gains, suggesting benefits not from capacity
Narrow experimental scope: only language modeling domains tested, brief autoregressive experiment shows minimal benefit, applicability to other architectures/modalities unclear
Incomplete mechanistic understanding: idle steps and oscillation issues are hypothesized explanations; temporal KL divergence is an indirect measure

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: The 'sampling wall' is clearly articulated and intuitively explained with concrete examples showing how distributional information collapses into one-hot vectors
Strong and consistent empirical results: 55-61% relative improvement in generative perplexity, gains across multiple frameworks (MDLM/UDLM), zero-shot transfer, and reasoning tasks
Simple and practical solution: Deterministic latent pathway requires only minor architectural modifications while maintaining training efficiency through self-conditioning

Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple metrics, thorough ablations, insightful analysis via temporal KL divergence and token-prediction entropy, scalability studies, and extensive reproducibility details
Methodological rigor: Matched computational budget experiments (Table 10) and isolation of latent propagation effects (Table 19) strengthen causal claims
Clear presentation: Well-written paper with effective visualizations of failure modes and generation quality improvements across baselines
weaknesses: Lack of theoretical framework: No rigorous mathematical justification for why latent propagation improves discrete diffusion; no analysis of ELBO or convergence properties; acknowledged gap in theoretical understanding
Limited core novelty: Self-conditioning is adapted from prior work (Chen et al. 2022, Jabri et al. 2022); main contribution is straightforward latent propagation without deep innovation

Insufficient justification of design choices: Stop-gradient on first pass is ad-hoc; multi-step backpropagation fails unexpectedly (Table 11) without investigation; self-conditioning probability p requires dataset-specific tuning (0.5-0.9 range)
Persistent gap with autoregressive models: 1.43× Gen PPL with MDLM, requires 512+ sampling steps to surpass AR baseline, making practical deployment unclear
Computational overhead: 30% training time increase and doubled embeddings for memory; cost/benefit tradeoff not thoroughly analyzed against alternatives
Scale limitations: Main experiments use modest architectures (768 hidden dims); scalability only tested to 424M parameters; unclear if gains hold at 7B+ scale
Incomplete scope: Only text and arithmetic tasks; minimal gains on autoregressive loopholing (D.4) suggest method specificity; no multimodal or broader applications

Evaluation concerns: G-Eval uses GPT-4 (not independent); no human evaluation; LDDM-U shows marginal improvements on many zero-shot benchmarks; generation quality still substantially below human-level
